verifier.theFinding: Pressing any key on a range in the right-hand panel leaves that panel's input dead for the next range that renders there. Waiting does not clear it, clicking the same panel does not clear it, operating a range in another panel does, and reloading does.
verifier.whatIsNotClaimed: This is a behavioural sequence, not a mechanism. No line of source was identified, and the reproduction uses selectObject(null) through the store API rather than the click-empty-space path a real user would take, so it is NOT claimed that a user can hit this. batch 695's 'unlocated' is replaced by 'located to a sequence, mechanism not traced' -- the distinction matters.
verifier.howToRead695: 695 blamed stage-to-stage carry-over in general terms. This batch names the carry-over: it is the keyboard, it is one press, and it survives time, repeated clicking and the same panel.

detail.whyElevenIsTheTruth: batch 695 measured this same control in a clean session and got 11 mouse-reachable values, K = 10.67, and two independent instruments agree. Eleven is the reading; one is the artefact.
detail.whatChanges: the ONLY difference between the two sessions is that one of them pressed a key on a range in the right-hand panel first.

the-bogus-reading-reproduces-and-a-clean.note: one press of one key is worth nine false values

detail.whyThisMatters: 'it settles after a while' was my first instinct and it is wrong. A time-based fix would have looked like it worked for four different wait lengths and then failed on the fifth run.

waiting-does-not-clear-it.note: a lock you can wait out is not a lock; this one is not

detail.whatHappened: This check failed on its first run, and the failure is the finding. An earlier run of the identical experiment reported 1 for both the one-click and the five-click case; this run reported 11 for both. Clicking the panel that received the key is therefore NOT a reliable way to clear the condition -- it sometimes works.
detail.consequence: The honest claim is 'clicking the same panel is not dependable', not 'clicking the same panel does not help'. Collapsing those two would put a rule in the ledger that the next reader will treat as settled.
detail.whatThisCheckDoesNotClaim: It asserts only that three repeats WITHIN one run agree. The cross-run disagreement (an earlier run gave 1 and 1 for the same two cases) is a fact this verifier cannot measure, because it would need the previous run's output as an input. It is recorded in the README and the ledger instead of being hidden in a name.
detail.whatRemainsReliable: The two recoveries that DID reproduce every time are the load-bearing ones: operating a range in another panel, and opening a fresh page. 695's fix is the second.

the-same-panel-recovery-gives-the-same-n.note: a behaviour that flips between runs is a weaker fact, and must be recorded as one

detail.whatThisPins: the condition is scoped to the right-hand panel, not to the page. A range outside that panel still works, and touching it restores the panel.

operating-a-range-in-another-panel-clear.note: the lock is local, and another panel is the key

detail.why695sFixIsEnough: 695's fix -- a fresh page per stage -- clears the condition by construction, which is why 695 ends at 6/6. This check confirms the fix addresses the condition rather than merely hiding it.

reloading-the-page-clears-it.note: 695's per-stage-page fix is sufficient, not a workaround
